points.description: Sets up the inversion at D (radius sqrt(DB·DC), possibly composed with reflection in D's line) and observes the inverse pairs: (A,H), (B,C), (E,F), (S,M), (Z,G), where Z is the reflection of R over AD (R and Z symmetric about AD). Equivalent correct identification of these correspondences earns the marks.

levels.says: Identifies only some of the inverse pairs or only the symmetry of R and Z, without justification of the inversion pairs.

points.description: Constructs the auxiliary point T (or a similar point on line AT) that is needed to translate the configuration, and uses it correctly toward identifying the images of the circles/points K, L, etc.
Shows that O and P are corresponding points under the inversion about D with radius sqrt(DB·DC) (O midpoint of DN, P on line DN on circle DKL), using the inverse relations of the earlier points.

Uses the inversion to show that the circle OCP maps to a circle/line through B and the image of P/O, hence that Q (second intersection of circle OCP with BC) is the inverse of a determined point with DB·DC = DQ·D(image), identifying Q's position on BC.
Concludes AB = AQ, e.g. by showing Q is the reflection of B over D or a point such that AD is the perpendicular bisector of BQ (or equivalent correct argument).

rubric.notes: Full marks need a complete valid proof; equivalent methods (not necessarily inversion) are accepted if rigorous. Part marks for the key observations (inverse pairs, construction of T, O and P as inverses). Zero for just restating the problem or numeric checks.
